thread:
anya: Quick thread - thoughts on a fallback auction when dedicated pool headroom is exhausted. I sketched two options: (A) immediate fallback to multi-tenant hosted with model-variant downgrade, (B) short auction of burst credits across tenants in the same shard to buy additional prewarmed slots.

matt: Interesting. Option A is simpler but risks data isolation/profile differences. Option B is more complex but keeps traffic local & cheaper. Need to weigh SLO impact.

tasha: For Option B, what does 'auction' mean operationally? synchronous call? background reconciler?

anya: Good Q. Idea: operator exposes `request_burst` RPC that returns either `granted` with node lease id or `queued` with estimated wait. Control plane runs an auction loop every 500ms to allocate available prewarm capacity to highest bid (bid is measured in burst credits + priority).

sam: Auction safety concerns: DoS risk if malicious tenants bid everything. Need per-tenant rate limits and a max-bid cap. Also audit logs.

lee: Also consider fairness - we should avoid starving low-cost tenants. Maybe a hybrid: half capacity allocated via strict priority, half via round-robin for small bids.

matt: I don't love complexity inside operator. Could we keep operator dumb: accept `prewarm_intent` with `bid_score` and let control plane run the auction and issue `prewarm_grant` token back to operator to actually allocate GPU? That keeps operator stateless.

tasha: That sounds better for private deployments where control plane may not be present. For private/on-prem we fall back to conservative behavior: deny auction and surface `fallback_allowed: true` so app can call hosted or use model-variant.

anya: Agreed. Let's sketch contract: `prewarm_intent {tenant, tokens, priority, bid_score, ttl_s}` -> operator persists ephemeral intent and emits `intent_event`. Control plane consumes events, runs auction, then sends back `grant {intent_id, node, lease_ttl}` or `deny {intent_id, reason}`. Operator then performs prewarm if grant.

sam: How do we meter costs? If tenant wins auction, charge burst credits + mark usage for billing export. Also record `auction_win_latency_ms`.

lee: Edge case: auction grant but node preempts before use. Need `grant_revoked` event and refund logic (partial or full). We should define refund policy: full refund if no connections observed within `use_window_s`.

matt: Observability: small set of metrics: `auction_attempts`, `auction_wins`, `auction_losses`, `grant_revocations`, `burst_credit_balance` (per-tenant hashed id), `fallback_count`. Dashboards per-tenant cohort + aggregate.

tasha: Privacy: again use `tenant_hash` by default. Also sample raw ids for high-severity incidents.

anya: Rollout idea: phase 0 = operator emits `intent_event` and metrics only. Phase 1 = control plane simulates auction and logs decisions (no-op grants). Phase 2 = enable real grants for canary tenants. Phase 3 = widen.

sam: Implementation constraints: auction loop needs determinism for debugging; use monotonic sequence + event-sourced state in control plane to reproduce decisions.

lee: On fairness, propose configurable shard-level knobs: `priority_share_pct` and `round_robin_share_pct`. Default 70/30.

matt: How about preemption semantics? If grant is given and a higher priority tenant later asks, do we preempt low-priority grant? We should avoid thrashing. Add grace window `min_use_window_s` before a grant can be evicted.

tasha: And `eviction_score` to pick eviction candidate: age, current inflight, priority, bid_score. Use simple weighted sum.

anya: Good. Also add accounting for `prewarm_warmup_ms` and `queued_wait_ms` for billing vs SLO.

sam: Testing: unit tests for auction logic, chaos test where nodes preempt mid-grant, and end-to-end with synthetic tenants to watch billing telemetry.

lee: For private deployments without control plane, operator should default to a policy: deny auction and offer `fallback_variant` suggestions (lower precision quantized models) so apps can continue. Document this in the operator README.

matt: One more thing: avoid global strong consistency for auction. Use shard-local auctions keyed by placement shard to limit blast radius and keep latency low.

an ya: small typo in my last msg^ :), agreed. So action items: anya to write operator event contract + metrics; matt to design control-plane auction service sketch; tasha to draft dashboards and SLOs; sam to enumerate security/rate-limit knobs; lee to write operator README fallback section. Can we all ack?

matt: ack

tasha: ack

sam: ack

lee: ack
